children: THE 60/40 PORTFOLIO IS WORKING AGAIN. THAT MAY NOT BE GOOD NEWS
US Treasuries are cushioning stock losses again, but that may not necessarily be good news, according to Nicholas Colas, co-founder of DataTrek Research.
peaked on October 6, it has lost 5.1%, and the Nasdaq
has dropped 11.1%. Over the same stretch, the Bloomberg US Aggregate Bond Index has risen 0.8%, and 7- to 10-year Treasuries have gained 1.3%.

For years, critics declared the 60/40 portfolio mix of stocks and bonds dead after the rate shock that began in 2022 led to the assets being increasingly correlated. But Colas says the period from 2022 to 2025 was a one-off reset in interest rates, not a structural break.

Negative stock-bond correlations often emerge when markets begin pricing in slower growth, Colas said. Bond prices gain as investors seek safety and anticipate Federal Reserve cuts, while equities weaken on the prospect of lower earnings estimates.

That does not make a recession inevitable; markets have a long record of sounding false alarms. But the renewed appeal of bonds may be an early warning that investors are becoming more cautious about the economy ahead.
